verdict.line: You lose if you let him land Q's empowered autos or his E stun in melee range; you win if you poke from Cannon-stance range and deny him a clean all-in window.

brief.thesis: Sett has no reliable ranged gap-closer outside E (Facebreaker, 490 range) and R (The Show Stopper, 400 range), so every point of distance you hold is damage he can't return. His passive (Pit Grit) heals him harder the lower his health drops and his Q (Knuckle Down) doubles his next two autos, which is why OP.GG flags lane sustain as his real strength, not burst. The matchup sits at an even 45.2% over 1911 games precisely because Jayce's 600-range poke counters that sustain only if he actually uses it instead of trading autos point-blank.

theirWindow.when: He lands E stun or Q's empowered autos
theirWindow.what: Sett's E (Facebreaker) only stuns if enemies are on both sides of him; if he catches you boxed in with minions on both flanks, you're stunned and his doubled Q autos will shred you. Disengage the instant E lands rather than trying to trade through it.

yourWindow.when: You're in Cannon stance at 600 range
yourWindow.what: Sit at max Q/W range in Cannon form and chip him with Shock Blast and Hyper Charge autos. He has nothing to punish this outside walking up or landing E/R, both of which you can see coming and step out of.

start.why: Picked in 95.4% of games for a reason — the extra sustain and early trade damage let you poke through Pit Grit's regen instead of losing the attrition war.

boots.why: Sett's passive is built entirely around alternating autos and Q's doubled-damage autos; flat armor directly undercuts the one way he can actually threaten you at range zero.

core.why: Builds mana sustain early so you can spam Q/W poke every wave without running dry, which is the whole point of out-ranging his sustain.
The active gives you a burst of speed to disengage the moment he closes distance with Q's move speed buff or walks up post-E.
Converts your mana into the raw poke damage that actually outpaces his Pit Grit regen over the course of a wave.
Highest win-rate finisher in this matchup (54.8% over 241 games) — the active lets you punish his engage attempts with a slow of your own.

situational.when: his Haymaker shield is soaking your poke damage
you need the slow to keep distance from his Q move speed chase
you want shield-break burst to force his W before he can all-in

runes.keystoneWhy: It rewards firing off three separate abilities then moving — exactly Jayce's Q/W/E poke rotation — and the move speed burst is what gets you out before his E (490 range) or R (400 range) can connect.

summoners.why: Ignite has the better measured win rate here (46.9%) because it directly cuts Pit Grit's missing-health regen, the exact sustain OP.GG calls out as his lane strength; Teleport (54.7% pick rate) is the safer alternative if you'd rather scale uncontested.

playing.title: Poke from Cannon stance
playing.detail: Stay in Cannon form at the edge of his lunge range and chip with Shock Blast and Hyper Charge autos — he has no reliable way to close that gap outside E and R.

playing.title: Never trade autos in melee
playing.detail: His passive heals off missing health and Q doubles his next two autos; standing still to right-click him back is the losing play every time.

playing.title: Hold position on E
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if he catches you between two bodies; stay on one side near your own minions so it slows instead, then punish the whiff.

playing.title: Swap to Hammer before his all-in
playing.detail: Transform back to Hammer stance ahead of his R windows (120/100/80/80/80s CD) so the bonus armor/MR and empowered first hit blunt the true damage from his W and the grab combo.

playing.title: Track his Grit bar
playing.detail: Haymaker's shield and true-damage punch scale with stored Grit; if he's been soaking your poke for several seconds, back off rather than fight into a full bar.

playing.title: Side-step his W, don't back straight up
playing.detail: The true damage lands in the center of Haymaker and physical on the sides, so stepping laterally keeps you in the weaker half of the hit.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning, power-curve calls, and lane plan are this brief's own analysis.
